resources.string: Watchpost could not start: %1$s\n\nNothing is being collected. If a Device Owner policy is applied, it can be undone from a computer with the rescue-revert script (ADB), then the app reinstalled (same signing key).
Permanent notification: Watchpost collects events on this device and sends them to your server.
not enrolled, everything stays on the device
This device is not enrolled: events are kept on the device (within the buffer limit) and nothing is uploaded.
Degraded mode: without Device Owner, network and security logs, automatic permission granting and force-stop protection are unavailable. It is enabled through ADB (see the README).
On Samsung, also add Watchpost to "Never sleeping apps" (Settings › Battery › Background usage limits): no API can do it automatically.

Watchpost only collects what is described in the Collectors tab, and every collector can be disabled. Events only go to the enrolled server, which you administer. The server cannot send the phone any configuration or policy, only commands from a closed list (the sensitive ones signed with a passphrase it does not know). No SMS, call, notification, keystroke or screen content is collected. The Local event log tab shows exactly what is emitted.
Every collector can be disabled. An "unavailable" collector is waiting for a permission, for Device Owner mode, or for hardware that is absent.
Experimental: behavior not guaranteed by Android
Latest events written by the agent since it started, as they will be uploaded. Tap an event to see all its data.
The 200 most recent events still in the device buffer.
Beyond it, the oldest and least severe events are deleted (reported by agent.buffer_overflow).
Unsent events older than this are deleted.
Periodic batch upload (15 min minimum). Severe events and the return of the network trigger an earlier upload.
On a metered network, if the buffer exceeds the threshold, only severe events are uploaded; the rest waits for an unmetered network.
Pending volume above which the Wi-Fi option applies.
Settings specific to each collector (cadences, filters, options) are in the Collectors tab, next to their switch.

Device Owner is removed from the Policy screen, or through ADB with "scripts/remove-device-owner.sh". A testOnly APK also allows a last resort, "adb shell dpm remove-active-admin", if Watchpost stops responding.

Choose the .watchpost file produced on your server (Docker install: "sudo ./enroll.sh phone" from the infra folder; standalone collector: "watchpost-collector enroll --name phone --out phone.watchpost"), copied over a cable, for example into Downloads. The private key is imported into the Android Keystore (non-exportable) and then forgotten; the token is encrypted on the device.
Pinned private CA (the only one accepted)
Device enrolled. The .watchpost file was deleted.
Device enrolled. Now delete the .watchpost file: it contains secrets.
Only the enrolled address receives data, over HTTPS with a client certificate. Redirects are refused, authorities added by the user are never accepted and cleartext traffic is forbidden.

The key, the certificate and the token will be erased, along with the %1$d events waiting to be uploaded. Collection continues locally.

resources.string: Renew without unenrolling: the client certificate expires (date above, 2 years after it was issued). Produce a new .watchpost file on the server and import it here: pending events are kept if it is the same server. "Unenroll", by contrast, erases the key, the token and the pending events.
Renewal: same server, same device. Pending events (%1$d) are kept.
Same server, different device identifier (%1$s → %2$s): pending events (%3$d) are kept and will be uploaded under the new identifier.
Different server (%1$s → %2$s): pending events (%3$d), collected for the old server, will be erased. Nothing collected for one server is ever sent to another.
